The primary bottleneck identified in AutoBuild's operational processes is the excessive travel time required for workers to retrieve tools and materials from a central repository. This inefficiency stems from the repository's location, which forces significant commutes across the work site, leading to lost productivity. To improve efficiency, the company should consider decentralizing the storage of tools and materials by establishing smaller, localized supply points closer to active construction zones. This would reduce transit time, minimize downtime, and allow workers to spend more time on actual construction tasks.
